headline: Chips Lead, Software Lags as Middle East Tensions Keep Markets Divided
body_html:
Tuesday's midday session is shaping up as a tale of two tapes. Semiconductors are the clear leader, advancing nearly 2% as a group, powered by Qualcomm's surge of more than 6% — the standout single-stock move of the day. United Microelectronics is adding close to 5% alongside it, reinforcing the sector's bid. Energy stocks are also finding support, up roughly 1%, with Bloom Energy climbing 6% to rank among the session's top performers. Breadth, however, is slightly negative: 280 names are in the red against 254 in the green across the 545-stock universe.

The dominant theme mid-session is geopolitical risk radiating from the Middle East. Houthi forces have struck four Saudi cities, disrupting energy infrastructure and wounding dozens, while Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic has slowed on fears of Iranian retaliation following recent U.S. military action. Brent crude is pressing toward $100 a barrel, keeping the energy sector bid even as questions persist about why the move has not been more dramatic given the scale of supply disruptions.

Healthcare and software are the day's laggards, falling 1.25% and 1.04% respectively. Sarepta Therapeutics is the session's worst performer by a wide margin, shedding nearly 13%. Into the close, watch whether the technology-sector ETF complex can hold its footing — a closely tracked signal for the durability of the broader bull market advance.

briefs.headline: Qualcomm Drives Semiconductor Surge to Session Highs
briefs.body: Qualcomm is up more than 6% at midday, anchoring a nearly 2% advance for the semiconductor sector — the strongest-performing group in Tuesday's session. United Microelectronics is contributing a gain of nearly 5%, suggesting broad participation across the chip complex rather than a single-name story.

briefs.headline: Sarepta Shares Crater, Healthcare Sector Takes the Day's Worst Hit
briefs.body: Sarepta Therapeutics is nursing a loss of nearly 13%, making it the sharpest decliner across the entire tracked universe on Tuesday. The biotech's slide is dragging the wider healthcare sector down 1.25%, the weakest sector reading of the session, with Incyte adding to the group's pain with a decline of roughly 3.6%.

briefs.headline: Houthi Strike on Saudi Cities Rattles Energy Markets
briefs.body: Houthi forces attacked four Saudi cities Tuesday, wounding 73 people and disrupting energy infrastructure, according to Reuters. The escalation is adding a risk premium to crude prices, with Brent approaching $100 a barrel and lifting energy equities roughly 1% on the session, led by Bloom Energy's 6% advance.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Slowdown Raises Supply-Disruption Alarm
briefs.body: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has decelerated after Iran threatened retaliation for recent U.S. military strikes, according to Reuters. The development has put global oil-supply routes on alert, contributing to currency pressure in India, where the rupee posted its steepest single-session drop in over a month as oil costs climbed.

briefs.headline: Software Names Slide as Growth Sentiment Softens
briefs.body: The software sector is off more than 1% at midday, with Datadog, Manhattan Associates, MongoDB, and Zscaler each falling between 3.6% and 3.9%. The synchronized weakness across observability, supply-chain, database, and security sub-segments points to a broad reassessment of growth-oriented software valuations rather than any single catalyst.

briefs.headline: Key Tech ETF Watched as Barometer for Bull Market's Next Move
briefs.body: Market observers are closely monitoring a widely followed technology ETF as a potential indicator of whether the current bull market advance has staying power, according to a midday analysis note. With semiconductors rallying and software retreating simultaneously, the ETF's intraday trajectory into the close is seen as a critical directional tell.
